voice_description: A 50-year-old American woman chatting candidly to a close friend from her parked car. Warm mid-low female register with a little lived-in grain and natural vocal fry. Clear neutral American accent. Relaxed, quick conversational delivery with varied inflection and connected phrases. Emotionally present, matter-of-fact about discomfort, gently skeptical, then relieved. Sounds like a real ordinary woman sharing something personal into her phone, with spontaneous human rhythm, not polished narration. Clean dry close microphone.
text: I was two months into a GLP-1, dropping weight, and still waking up every morning feeling backed up and uncomfortable like nothing had moved. Let me tell you what I finally found out. Because nobody told me about it either. Because I was dropping weight. The shot was actually working. But I felt like someone had filled my gut with concrete and forgotten about it. That heavy backed-up pressure that just sat there all day. I'd eat a few bites at dinner and feel like I'd swallowed a brick. And it didn't matter how little I ate. It just kept building.
